decisions.reason: Although this adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display fits our existing display know-how well, its disappearance from website promotion after 2019 in a flat market suggests limited durable traction, so we would fold any learning back into the core range and redeploy resources.

This pegboard-back cardboard shelf display is close to our established capabilities, but the lack of visible continuation beyond 2019 indicates that the market response was not strong enough to justify keeping a separate product line.

Because this standard cardboard quarter-pallet display is highly related to what we already do, we can absorb its design lessons into existing offerings, and its short observed market life points to dropping it as a standalone product.

The eighth-pallet cardboard display is technically close to our core business, yet the absence of continued market presentation after 2019 implies insufficient momentum, so we would discontinue it and concentrate on stronger core formats.

The wooden display pallet is only adjacent to our paper-based knowledge base and appears not to have sustained visible market support beyond 2019, so absorptive-capacity logic favors exiting it rather than investing further in a less related material platform.

This media-focused cardboard quarter-pallet display is related to our existing expertise, but its limited observed persistence suggests that the niche did not warrant ongoing dedicated investment, so we would drop it and retain only the know-how gained.
